title: The Call of the Wild
subtitle: Instinct, faith, and a turn of fate—that's all it takes to succeed.

items.text: The Call of the Wild

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: That's odd.
Antarctic Plain
Nautika looks down at her map, then up at the surrounding snow slopes and peaks. She repeats this several times, searching for familiar landmarks.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Are we lost?

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: My team reached the outer perimeter of the ruins twice. The entrance should be right around here.
She rubs her gloved hands together, the fabric rustling softly.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: S-Sorry, Vertin. The terrain here is nothing like I remember.

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: Just so you know, I've lost all radio reception from the Foundation.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: No signal, no landmarks, no working compass, and the terrain doesn't match what's on the map.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: What should we do now, Timekeeper?
Their energetic sled dogs, after only a brief rest in the snow, start chasing each other's tails.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Hey! Hey! My watch is not for dogs! Give me that! Shoo, shoo!
Nautika wipes the drool off her antique watch before storing it safely in her pack.
The dogs play in an Ouroboros-like circle, happy whimpers filling the air.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I have an idea. In fact, the answer's right in front of us.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Shh. Watch.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Dr. Dores's stethoscope?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Ah. You're right. It's been staring us right in the face.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: The sled dogs are canines after all. They should have a sensitive sense of smell.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Yes, if we give them a moment to smell the stethoscope, they may be able to track down the scent left on it. Let's hope it works.
The lead dog releases its companion's soggy tail and lowers its snout to sniff the stethoscope.

items.speaker: Sled Dog
items.text: Woof! Woof woof!

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: They—They smelled something!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Hop on their backs.
The daylight that shines on this hinterland stretches into eternity.
Movement across the icy wastes seems meaningless without reference points, just as none could say how long the sled dogs run before their sudden halt.
Stone Labyrinth

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: We made it. This is where my team went before.
She pulls the harness, and the sled dogs obey in a steady and contented stop.

items.speaker: Ear Worm Máhtu
items.text: "The guide appears, then fades from human sight; If the devoted journey, let their songs unite."

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Máhtu was right. The Mother Spirit was right. It was the right decision to join you.
The companions pat the dogs as they dismount.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Where are we? A labyrinth in a valley?

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Friele believed that these were the only outskirts of the site. She said that if we passed through the valley, we might even find the real ruins of a temple, or a city even.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Look at this stone wall. There are excavation marks on it.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: We ran into an abnormal whiteout last time. It was too dense. We couldn't make out any details.
She sprints to the nearest rock face, crouches, strips off a glove, and presses her warm palm against the frozen stone.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I've never seen this kind of rock before. Is it some kind of fossil?

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: It's tholeiitic basalt. It forms at mid-ocean ridges, down at the bottom of the sea. Look at the geometric pores and the golden mineral veins.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: If Friele were here, she'd call it a miracle. A once-in-a-425-million-year occurrence.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Friele ... heh. She would have been so excited to see this, even if it is only the size of my palm. That's why she joined the expedition.
Head bowed, she warms the rock before slipping it into her pocket,
as if cradling some cherished lifeform.
After a faint tremor, the arcane fluctuation dissolves into flying snow pellets.
Instinct carries her two steps forward before freezing.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper?
Her sight has locked onto an anomalous snow mound at the base of the opposite rock face.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Not an illusion.
Crouching, she brushes away the accumulated powder.
A portable vintage typewriter.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I read about this typewriter in the file. Ms. White Rum and Nala also mentioned it.
In this era, it typed terse medical records for the drowning girl, recorded São Paulo's raucous nights, and bore witness to Ushuaia's poetry society.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: That's right. This is Dr. Dores's typewriter.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Another one of her belongings. Is it too coincidental to be mere chance?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: *cough* What's this all over it? Scale powder?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Blood. It's dry.
Penguins, seals, or the fallen at the research station.
The bloodstains could belong to anyone, including Doctor Dores.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Whether these were left intentionally or not, this proves that we're heading in the right direction.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: So much blood. She may be injured. We need to find her as soon as possible.
Everyone crowds around, including Ms. Radio, who had been lying on one of the dogs.
Barren mountains flank them on both sides, a stone labyrinth of basalt standing sentinel at the pass, its end shrouded in mist.
The lead dog approaches, then raises its head, alerted to some unseen threat.

items.speaker: Sled Dog
items.text: Woof! Woof woof!

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: Wait!

items.speaker: Ms. Radio
items.text: Holy—! Where are you taking me?

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: Stop! Whoa!
Nautika presses two fingers to her lips and issues sharp whistle commands.

items.speaker: Sled Dog
items.text: Woof! Woof—
Their paws churn the soft snow, drowning out the whistle commands meant for the loyal friends.
The excited sled dogs charge into the labyrinth, carrying the helpless Ms. Radio with them, and soon disappear from view.

items.speaker: Nautika
items.text: They're gone. W-What do we do now?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Think positively. Perhaps they'll just get there before us. Let's go after them.
Their movement triggers something hidden, causing the snowfield around them to shake.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Wait, there are critters hiding out nearby.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: There they are. Timekeeper, watch out!
